rows.answer: An appeal is a request to have a decision about your Social Security benefits or SSI reviewed. If you were recently denied, you generally have 60 days after you receive the notice of the decision to ask for any type of appeal. There are four levels of appeal: Reconsideration, Hearing by an administrative law judge, Review by the Appeals Council, and Federal Court review. A reconsideration is a complete review of your claim by someone who did not take part in the first determination, and Social Security will look at all the evidence submitted in the original determination plus any new evidence. You can request an appeal online for a reconsideration, a hearing by an administrative law judge, and a review by the Appeals Council.

rows.answer: To file a complaint against your school, the appropriate route depends on the issue. If you believe your school is not administering federal student aid funds properly (for example, calculating your eligibility incorrectly, disbursing aid incorrectly, lacking required policies, or making false or misleading statements), and you have already tried to resolve it with the school, you may contact the Federal Student Aid Feedback Center or call 1-844-651-0077. If you suspect your school or an individual of fraud, waste, or abuse involving federal student aid, you can make a confidential report to ED’s Office of Inspector General Fraud Hotline. If you believe the school misrepresented its educational program, cost, outcomes, or recruitment practices, you can also contact the Federal Student Aid Feedback Center. If you think your school awarded aid to someone else in your name, report it to the Office of Inspector General Hotline as identity theft.
citations: Aid for Military Families | Federal Student Aid#1_0::chunk-3
